quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Use only your rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move.
Use only your left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check for cars in your blind spot. Check multiple times before changing lanes. Watch traffic in front of you and in the lane next to you.

questions.question: The car ahead stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Slowly pass the car at 10 mph or less.
Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes and pass the stopped car carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a stopped car at a crosswalk. Pedestrians you cannot see may be crossing. Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have crossed.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. How can you prevent it in wet weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the road's shoulder when rain starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down when the road is wet to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Get ready for traffic to merge into your lane.
Always stop.
Divided highway ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready for traffic to merge into your lane.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that cars will merge from the right. Be ready to let them merge safely.

questions.question: What sign is this?

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A downward-pointing triangle is always a yield sign. You must be ready to slow down or stop at a yield sign.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming cars are going. They may seem slower than they actually are. Make sure you have enough space to pass safely. If you are unsure about an oncoming car's speed, wait to pass.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness.
Coordination.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many driving skills. They affect reaction time, coordination, alertness, and the ability to concentrate.

questions.question: What does this white sign mean?

options.text: The railroad crossing is controlled. Drive at your normal speed.
Look, listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
Stop at the tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Let any trains pass before you go.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is safe.
Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
Your driving speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous because it frustrates drivers behind you. They may make risky moves to pass. Drive with the flow of traffic within the speed limit.

questions.question: When driving near a large truck, what should you do?

options.text: Follow closely to reduce wind drag on your car.
Avoid staying beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid staying beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots on each side. Do not stay beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast a person absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A person's weight affects alcohol absorption. Other factors include biological sex, how much food is in the stomach, and how many drinks have been consumed. The only way to remove alcohol from the body is to wait.

questions.question: A five-sided sign is a:

options.text: Stop sign.
Regulatory sign.
School zone or school crossing sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or school crossing sign.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign warns drivers about school zones. Some of these signs mark crosswalks in school zones where children or pedestrians may cross.

questions.question: Which statement is true about large trucks?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
They all have air brakes that stop them quickly.
They are easier to turn than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than passenger vehicles. A passenger vehicle going 55 mph stops in about 400 feet. A large truck going the same speed needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. Turning right here is unsafe and against the law.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow down to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic flow, and merge when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic flow, and merge when safe.
questions.explanation: Do not stop when entering an interstate. Instead, use the merging lane to speed up and match the speed of traffic already on the highway. Then merge smoothly when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a red eight-sided sign say?

options.text: Do not enter.
One-way.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means "stop." You must come to a complete stop at this sign.

questions.question: A green arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: You must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.
You may turn in the direction shown after coming to a complete stop.
You cannot turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means traffic in that lane must proceed in the direction shown. You have the right-of-way when turning on a green arrow, but always watch for pedestrians and other vehicles.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Do not enter.
Yield the right-of-way.
Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is posted on one-way streets and roads where you are not allowed to enter. You may see this sign if you try to enter an expressway ramp the wrong way.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. You may turn left onto another one-way street only if:

options.text: You speed up before the turn.
Traffic on that street moves to the right.
Traffic on that street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic on that street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street if traffic moves to the left and no sign prohibits it. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Follow the car ahead more closely.
Pass through carefully and do not stare at the construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass through carefully and do not stare at the construction.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at unusual things. This is called "rubbernecking" and causes traffic congestion in construction zones.

questions.question: At a yield sign, you must:

options.text: Let other traffic pass if they are close enough to cause a crash.
Let vehicles only on your right pass.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic pass if they are close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must let traffic in the lanes you want to enter pass first. You should be ready to stop. If there is no traffic, you may continue without stopping.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Do not turn right.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not turn right.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits right turns. You cannot turn right at this intersection.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Look behind you, then check the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let other vehicles move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look behind you, then check the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, check for vehicles beside and behind you. Make sure the lane you want to enter is clear.

questions.question: Which road is most likely to be icy after snow or rain?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A road in shade

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in shade
questions.explanation: Shaded areas on the road freeze before other areas and thaw out later. Watch for ice in shaded spots on cold, wet days.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Use low beam headlights.
Use high beam headlights until you are 10 feet from the vehicle ahead.
Use high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when following another vehicle. High beams should only be used in rural areas when other cars are not nearby.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A divided highway is ending.
A divided highway is starting.
The road ahead is slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is starting.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway begins ahead. Stay to the right of the center divider.

questions.question: Truck blind spots are located:

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
To the immediate left of the cab.
Both directly behind the truck and to the immediate left of the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both directly behind the truck and to the immediate left of the cab.
questions.explanation: Trucks have large blind spots. The driver cannot see vehicles directly behind them or to the left of the cab. If you cannot see the driver's face in their mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: When roads are slippery after rain begins, you should:

options.text: Avoid fast turns and stops.
Test your tire traction while going uphill.
Look closer to your vehicle instead of ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid fast turns and stops.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire grip. Slow down on wet roads and avoid sudden turns or stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice with Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press the brake pedal firmly and hold it.
Stay off the brakes and let the car slide to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal firmly and hold it.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly when stopping on snow or ice. The ABS system will pump the brakes for you faster than you can.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.
Stop sign ahead.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that wet pavement can cause you to lose control. Slow down when you see this sign because it takes longer to stop on wet roads.
